answer: Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 514 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. Because the sparrow height is fixed at intake and published in the sable receipt, the fable audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which burns it the epoch. That is 29 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
